items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: They thought that the blues was Ted Lewis and they thought that was a corny remark that I made... because they were identifying with something Ted Lewis did, Blues My Naughty Sweetie Gives Me.

ctx.x: Well, something in the sense of Fletcher being Benny's -- gave

Well, there is no doubt about it. You see, Benny Goodman started a long time before I did and of course, Benny Goodman compared to me, I mean, Benny Goodman was a true genius, at the age of 12 he was a superb clarinet, and I remember -- he was not as involved in jazz as I was, and I remember one time playing with the Pollack band in New York, and we were all sitting around, Glenn Miller, Benny Goodman, Ben Pollack -- But Ben Pollack knew, and I happened to say -- we were talking about a player and I said, 'Well,…

was something. But Benny Goodman and Glenn Miller didn't. This is 1928 I am talking about. They were putting me on because I mentioned the blues, because they were identifying with something Ted Lewis did, Blues My Naughty Sweetie Gives Me.
